description_good_justification: README.md opens with a one-line description ('C2PA soft binding and content fingerprinting for text assets (watermark + fingerprint family)') and an Overview section explaining what the crate does and why.
interact_justification: README.md documents installation (crates.io/npm/PyPI, 'Quick Start'), links to SECURITY.md for vulnerability reports, and CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to submit issues and PRs via GitHub.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' section: fork, branch from main, make changes, open a PR. Confirmed by actual merged PR history (e.g. gh pr list shows PRs #3-#21 merged via the normal GitHub PR flow).
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md specifies acceptance requirements: run `cargo test --all-features`, `cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and use Conventional Commits style.
floss_license_justification: Cargo.toml: license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"; both are FLOSS licenses per OSI/FSF.
floss_license_osi_justification: LICENSE-APACHE (Apache License 2.0) and LICENSE-MIT (MIT License) are both OSI-approved licenses; verified by reading the actual license text headers in LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT.
license_location_justification: LICENSE-APACHE and LICENSE-MIT hold the full texts (dual MIT OR Apache-2.0 per Cargo.toml); a top-level LICENSE file (identical to LICENSE-APACHE) is also present at the repository root for tooling that only recognizes that exact filename.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md covers overview, install, quick start with code examples, algorithm table, and links to ROBUSTNESS.md, TRANSPORT.md, STABILITY.md for deeper docs. docs.rs badge indicates generated API docs (all-features enabled per [package.metadata.docs.rs] in Cargo.toml).
documentation_interface_justification: Public API is documented via rustdoc (#![warn(missing_docs)] in src/lib.rs enforces doc comments) and published to docs.rs; README.md documents the external CBOR/COSE assertion format and gives worked input/output code examples for soft_binding, sign_cose, and verify.
sites_https_justification: Repo URL is https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-text-binding; all README links (crates.io, docs.rs, writerslogic.com, spec.c2pa.org) use https://.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled and public (gh issue list shows issues #1-#2), URL-addressable at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-text-binding/issues, open to any GitHub user, no proprietary client required.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, ROBUSTNESS.md, TRANSPORT.md, STABILITY.md) and commit messages observed in `git log` are in English.
maintained_justification: `git log` shows commits through 2026-08-22 (most recent: 0abd203, docs updates); gh repo view shows pushedAt 2026-08-24T13:12:17Z. 65 total commits (`git rev-list --count HEAD`), active within the last 60 days.
repo_public_justification: gh repo view shows isPrivate: false at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-text-binding.
repo_track_justification: Git repo with full commit history (`git log` shows author, date, message per commit; `git rev-list --count HEAD` = 65 commits).
repo_interim_justification: `git log --oneline` shows many commits between the v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 tags (e.g. cfc4228, 92dc7c6, 90c15e5, 6c03acc, and others), not just tagged release commits.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses git, a distributed VCS (confirmed via .git directory and git commands run against the repo).
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml version = "0.3.0"; release.yml validates that the pushed git tag (vX.Y.Z) matches Cargo.toml's version before publishing, guaranteeing unique per-release identifiers.
version_semver_justification: Cargo.toml uses SemVer (0.3.0); git tags v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 (`git tag -l`) follow vX.Y.Z; release.yml regex-validates tags as ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-...)?$.
version_tags_justification: `git tag -l` shows v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 as annotated release points in the VCS.
release_notes_justification: release.yml generates human-readable release notes via git-cliff (cliff.toml config, 'Generate release notes' step producing RELEASE_NOTES.md) attached to each GitHub release, not a raw commit log dump.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly disclosed vulnerabilities with CVEs have been fixed in this project's history to date (no entries in SECURITY.md or GitHub Security Advisories observed), so there is nothing to identify in release notes.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is used for bug reports; .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml provide structured templates, and CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Issues' points to them.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used as the tracker; gh issue list shows individually tracked issues (#1, #2) with labels (documentation, good first issue).
report_responses_justification: Both issues on record (#1 'Add doc-tests for the fingerprinting trait', #2 'Document fingerprint stability guarantees') are CLOSED as of 2026-08-03, indicating they were acted on. Sample size is small (2 issues total), but both were addressed.
enhancement_responses_justification: Both tracked issues were enhancement/documentation-type requests and both were closed/resolved (see gh issue list output), consistent with responsiveness, though the sample is only 2 issues.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a public, searchable archive of all reports and responses at https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-text-binding/issues (includes closed issues #1, #2).
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents the process: GitHub Security Advisories (private) or email admin@writerslogic.com, explicitly stating not to use public issues.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md explains private reporting via GitHub Security Advisories (https://github.com/writerslogic/c2pa-text-binding/security/advisories/new) or direct email to admin@writerslogic.com.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months (no advisories or SECURITY.md changelog entries found), so there is no response-time data to evaluate.
build_justification: Cargo is the automated build system; `cargo build` and `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` are run in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml, release.yml), and maturin builds the Python wheels (release.yml pypi-wheels job).
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo, the standard Rust build tool, plus wasm-pack and maturin, both standard/common tools for their respective Rust-to-wasm and Rust-to-Python-wheel targets.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, wasm-pack, and maturin are all FLOSS tools; no proprietary build tooling is used per Cargo.toml, ci.yml, and release.yml.
test_justification: FLOSS test suite via `cargo test` (tests/c2pa_roundtrip.rs, tests/fail_safety.rs, tests/false_positive.rs, tests/interop.rs, tests/jumbf_payload.rs, plus unit tests in src/, ~82 #[test]/proptest! items total). Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md ('cargo build && cargo test') and run in ci.yml.
test_invocation_justification: Tests are invoked with the standard Rust convention `cargo test`, as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and used in .github/workflows/ci.yml's 'test' job.
test_most_justification: Test suite includes unit tests per module, integration tests (c2pa_roundtrip.rs, interop.rs, fail_safety.rs, false_positive.rs, jumbf_payload.rs), and property-based tests via the `proptest` dev-dependency (Cargo.toml), covering normal, edge-case, and adversarial/failure-mode inputs.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs 'test', 'check' (clippy/fmt), and 'msrv' jobs on every push to main and every pull request.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Submitting Changes' step 2 explicitly states: 'Make changes, add tests, run cargo test --all-features.'
tests_are_added_justification: Recent commits show tests added alongside functionality, e.g. commit 90c15e5 'feat: uniform Error::code, verified MSRV, and integration tests' and f79576f 'docs: state and test the fingerprint stability guarantees' (git log).
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the test-addition policy directly in the contribution instructions (step 2 of 'Submitting Changes').
warnings_justification: clippy (FLOSS Rust linter) is enabled in CI: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy --lib --features python -- -D warnings`; src/lib.rs also sets `#![warn(missing_docs)]`.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI uses `-D warnings` (deny), which fails the build on any clippy warning, so warnings cannot merge unaddressed; ci.yml 'check' job enforces this on every push/PR.
warnings_strict_justification: `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` denies (not just warns on) all default clippy lints across all targets, and separately for the python feature, which is close to maximal strictness practical for a published, cross-target (native/wasm/python) crate.
know_secure_design_justification: SECURITY.md documents supply-chain hardening (GitHub Actions pinned to full SHAs, Scorecard, Dependabot) and the codebase shows deliberate secure-design choices: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] in src/lib.rs, constant-time comparison (ct_eq in src/stego.rs) for tag verification, and dedicated crypto library use (ed25519-dalek, sha2, hmac) rather than reimplementation.
know_common_errors_justification: Evidence of awareness of vulnerability classes specific to this domain: constant-time tag comparison to avoid timing side-channels (src/stego.rs ct_eq), HMAC-based integrity checking discussed in README.md ('A.8 needs a checksum... an integrity field... fails safe'), and security-focused commits (2466dba 'pin the harness base image and pip installs by hash', c228c59 'bump pyo3 to 0.29', add05ed 'pin actions by SHA and drop GITHUB_TOKEN to read').
crypto_published_justification: Only publicly published/reviewed algorithms are used by default: Ed25519 (ed25519-dalek), SHA-256/512 (sha2), HMAC (hmac), BLAKE2 (blake2), per Cargo.toml dependencies and src/manifest.rs, src/stego.rs.
crypto_call_justification: Crypto functionality calls dedicated, audited crates (ed25519-dalek, sha2, hmac, blake2, coset for COSE) rather than reimplementing primitives; confirmed in Cargo.toml and src/manifest.rs (`use ed25519_dalek::{Signature, Signer, SigningKey, Verifier, VerifyingKey}`).
crypto_floss_justification: All crypto dependencies (sha2, hmac, blake2, ed25519-dalek, coset, ciborium) are FLOSS Rust crates; src/lib.rs states 'All cryptography is pure Rust with no C bindings'.
crypto_keylength_justification: Ed25519 (32-byte/256-bit keys, ~128-bit security level) is used for signing via ed25519-dalek; this meets NIST-equivalent strength recommendations through 2030. No configurable smaller/weaker key size is exposed.
crypto_working_justification: No MD4/MD5/single-DES/RC4/Dual_EC_DRBG found in Cargo.toml dependencies or src/*.rs (verified by grep); default algorithms are Ed25519/SHA-256/SHA-512/HMAC/BLAKE2.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or CBC mode found in Cargo.toml or src/*.rs (verified by grep); hashing uses SHA-256/512 (sha2 crate) and BLAKE2, and signing uses Ed25519 (EdDSA, not CBC-based).
crypto_pfs_justification: The crate performs static message signing (Ed25519/COSE_Sign1 over a soft-binding assertion, src/manifest.rs) rather than a session/key-agreement protocol, so perfect forward secrecy does not apply.
crypto_password_storage_justification: This crate performs content fingerprinting and C2PA manifest signing; it has no user accounts or password storage anywhere in src/ (verified by grep and file inspection).
crypto_random_justification: The crate does not generate cryptographic keys or nonces itself: README.md's example shows the Ed25519 secret_key as caller-supplied ('// caller-supplied Ed25519 secret'), and no key-generation function exists in src/manifest.rs (only SigningKey::from_bytes on a caller-provided array). The HMAC-seeded xorshift PRNG in src/stego.rs (fisher_yates/next_rand) is a deterministic placement permutation for watermark reversibility, not a security key/nonce.
delivery_mitm_justification: Package delivery is via crates.io, npm, and PyPI, all served over HTTPS; release.yml publishes via `cargo publish`, `npm publish` (registry-url https://registry.npmjs.org), and PyPI trusted publishing (OIDC, no long-lived token over plaintext).
delivery_unsigned_justification: No unsigned hash-only integrity check is retrieved over plain HTTP; all package registries (crates.io, npm, PyPI) are accessed via HTTPS, and release.yml additionally attests build provenance for the npm tarball via actions/attest-build-provenance.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No open, unpatched medium+ severity vulnerabilities are evident; Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml) runs weekly across cargo, github-actions, and docker ecosystems, and recent security-labeled commits (2466dba, c228c59, ebe61fc) show prompt remediation, e.g. ebe61fc 'autofix 3rd party Github Actions should be pinned' merged as PR #14 same day it was opened (2026-08-03).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: git log shows security fix commits (2466dba, c228c59, add05ed) landing promptly; PR #14 (Aikido AI security fix for unpinned GitHub Actions) was opened and merged on the same day (2026-08-03 per gh pr list).
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Grep for private-key markers, API key/secret assignment patterns, and AWS key patterns across *.rs/*.toml/*.md found no matches. Secrets used in CI (CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN) are referenced only as ${{ secrets.* }} GitHub Actions secrets in release.yml, never inline.
static_analysis_justification: clippy, a FLOSS static analysis tool for Rust, is run in ci.yml ('check' job: `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the python-feature variant) on every push and PR, i.e. before any release.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: clippy's default lint set includes correctness and suspicious-pattern lints that catch common vulnerability-adjacent bugs (integer overflow patterns, unsafe misuse, etc.); additionally OpenSSF Scorecard (.github/workflows/scorecard.yml) runs supply-chain/vulnerability-relevant checks and uploads SARIF to GitHub code scanning.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI enforces `-D warnings` (deny), so any clippy finding blocks merge until fixed; git log shows dedicated fix commits addressing tool findings, e.g. ebe61fc 'fix(security): autofix 3rd party Github Actions should be pinned' resolving an Aikido SAST finding (PR #14).
static_analysis_often_justification: ci.yml runs clippy on every push to main and every pull request (not just before releases), per the `on: push/pull_request` triggers in .github/workflows/ci.yml.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (e.g. fuzzing via cargo-fuzz, sanitizers) is configured in any workflow under .github/workflows/ or referenced in Cargo.toml; only proptest (property-based testing, not a dynamic analysis/fuzzing harness in the OpenSSF sense) is present as a dev-dependency.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: src/lib.rs declares `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, so there is no memory-unsafe (unsafe Rust/C/C++) code in this crate to analyze with a memory-safety dynamic tool.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis configuration exists (see dynamic_analysis above), so there is no assertion-enabling config to evaluate.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is currently applied (see dynamic_analysis above), so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to have fixed.
